newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso seeks reform votes this year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso seeks reform votes this year.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Friday he hoped the lower house and Senate would complete this year votes on a civil service reform bill and a social security reform bill.

Cardoso told foreign journalists in Brasilia he was working hard to ensure the Chamber dealt with the administrative reforms by year-end and that the Senate successfully revamped a pension system bill that was watered down in the lower house.
"I think the administrative reforms are the most urgent issue at the moment. I hope the lower house will vote this year," Cardoso said.
He added, "The (bill) has already been the subject of ample negotiation in Congress."
The civil service reforms, which have languished in Congress while attention focused on municipal elections earlier in November, must go to the Senate once approved by the Chamber.

Cardoso said the pension reform bill approved by the lower house was "insufficient", especially in regard to the public sector, and that he hoped the Senate would have reformulated the law by the end of 1996.
"I am striving hard in the Chamber and the Senate for the votes to take place this year. I don't know whether I will succeed, but I will try," Cardoso said.
